title: Building AI Agents in ServiceNow: A Complete Guide
excerpt: Learn how to create intelligent AI agents that automate complex workflows using ServiceNow's AI capabilities and GenAI integration.
content:
Introduction

AI Agents are revolutionizing how enterprises handle automation. In this guide, we'll explore how to build intelligent agents within ServiceNow that can reason, decide, and act autonomously.

What are AI Agents?

AI Agents are autonomous systems that can perceive their environment, make decisions, and take actions to achieve specific goals. In ServiceNow, these agents can handle everything from incident resolution to complex approval workflows.

Getting Started

To build an AI Agent in ServiceNow, you'll need:

  • ServiceNow Utah or later
  • AI Control Tower access
  • Integration Hub subscription

Implementation Steps

First, configure your AI Control Tower settings to enable agent capabilities. Then create a new AI Agent definition:

// Sample GlideRecord script for AI Agent
var gr = new GlideRecord('sn_ai_agent');
gr.initialize();
gr.name = 'Incident Resolution Agent';
gr.active = true;
gr.insert();

This foundation allows you to build sophisticated automation that learns and adapts over time.

title: GenAI Summarization for Risk Management
excerpt: How I implemented GenAI-powered summarization in ServiceNow's Risk Workspace to reduce analysis time by 60%.
content:
The Challenge

Risk analysts were spending hours reading through lengthy risk assessments and compliance documents. We needed a solution that could summarize key points instantly while maintaining accuracy.

The Solution

By integrating GenAI capabilities with ServiceNow's GRC module, we created an automated summarization system that processes documents in real-time.

Architecture

The system uses a three-tier approach:

  • Document ingestion via Integration Hub
  • GenAI processing with custom prompts
  • Results displayed in Risk Workspace widget

Results

The implementation reduced analysis time by 60% and improved risk detection accuracy by identifying patterns human analysts often missed.

title: Flow Designer Best Practices for Enterprise Scale
excerpt: Essential patterns and anti-patterns when building flows that need to handle thousands of executions daily.
content:
Why Flow Designer Matters

Flow Designer is ServiceNow's powerful low-code automation tool. But with great power comes great responsibility—especially at enterprise scale.

Best Practices

  • Use Subflows: Break complex logic into reusable subflows
  • Error Handling: Always implement try-catch patterns
  • Async Operations: Use async for heavy processing
  • Monitoring: Track execution times and failures

Anti-Patterns to Avoid

Don't create flows that query large datasets without filters. Always use indexed fields and limit result sets.

// Bad: Queries all incidents
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.query();

// Good: Filtered query
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident');
gr.addQuery('state', 1);
gr.addQuery('sys_created_on', '>=', gs.daysAgo(7));
gr.setLimit(100);
gr.query();

title: The Future of Enterprise AI: 2025 Trends
excerpt: Exploring the emerging trends in enterprise AI adoption and what it means for ServiceNow developers.
content:
Enterprise AI in 2025

The enterprise AI landscape is evolving at an unprecedented pace. Here are the key trends shaping the industry this year.

Trend 1: Agentic AI

The shift from simple automation to intelligent agents that can reason, plan, and execute complex tasks autonomously. These agents don't just follow rules—they adapt to situations.

Trend 2: AI Governance

With great AI power comes great responsibility. Enterprises are investing heavily in AI Control Towers and governance frameworks to ensure responsible AI deployment.

What This Means for ServiceNow

ServiceNow is well-positioned to capitalize on these trends with its Now Platform AI capabilities, including Now Assist and AI Control Tower. Developers who master these tools will be in high demand.
